newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo, rebel leader swap letters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo, rebel leader swap letters.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-12-09

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo and Zapatista rebel leader Subcommander Marcos have swapped letters in an unusual gesture aimed at shoring up troubled peace efforts.

In a letter sent Sunday to Zedillo, Marcos agreed to give the government 15 days to study a rebel proposal for constitutional changes strengthening Indian rights. The text of his letter was made available to Reuters on Monday.
Zedillo had written to Marcos last week asking for the delay and emphasising his government's commitment to peace.

The pipe-smoking rebel praised the Yale-educated Zedillo for writing and getting "personally involved" in the peace process, which has been flagging since rebels broke off talks with government envoys in September.

The Zapatistas and a legislative commission had already hammered out the constitutional changes to be made, and were angered last week when central government officials said they would have to review them. Marcos said the peace process was in yet another crisis.

dc.value: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico
